name: Step Denver
bednote: Primary facility: 65; sober homes bring the published total to 95
cost: Free entry; program fees and food expenses after employment.
residency: Out-of-state applicants considered; arrange intake before travel.
stay: No fixed stay; continued participation and employment required.
details: Bed count

The organization's ColoradoGives profile lists 65 beds at the primary facility and room for up to 95 men including sober homes. An operator-published July 2025 article also describes the 65-bed Denver facility. This replaces the earlier 60-bed figure from 2023. The 95 total is not the size of the entry facility; neither figure is a vacancy count.
Cost and stay

No entry charge is published. After employment, Step lists $15/day, $75/week, or $200/month in program fees, plus buying and preparing food. Confirm the applicable payment option. There is no fixed stay length.
Admission and work

Applications normally run Monday-Friday, 7 a.m.-noon. Out-of-state intake exceptions are possible. Applicants must be sober at intake and able to work a full-time payroll job. The operator lists restrictions on outside financial support and government stipends. This is not a clinical detox service; confirm all medications and screening rules.

name: Sage Ridge
bednote: 192 recovery-housing places at full capacity; clinical beds counted separately
cost: Housing reported free; confirm separate healthcare costs.
residency: Colorado eligibility rules conflict between the webpage and application. Call intake.
stay: Up to two years; referral and screening required.
warning: The webpage says Colorado residency OR Colorado Medicaid; the August 2026 application asks for six months in Colorado.
details: Bed count

The operator's March 2026 fact sheet lists 192 recovery-housing places at full capacity. AllHealth Network separately lists 27 withdrawal-management beds on campus. Those clinical beds are excluded from this housing count and cost statement. Capacity does not establish current openings or staffed beds.
Residency: confirmation needed

The current operator webpage says Colorado residency or Colorado Medicaid. Its linked application, revised August 31, 2026, asks applicants to attest to six months living, renting, or attending school in Colorado; it does not show a Medicaid exception. The sources do not resolve which rule governs an individual application. Ask intake before arranging travel.
Cost and admission

January 2026 reporting quotes a Coalition spokesperson describing Sage Ridge and Fort Lyon as free to guests. Confirm housing terms, benefit contributions and separate medical charges. Adults must be experiencing homelessness or housing instability, voluntarily pursuing recovery and medically stable for independent daily living. Legal and medical screening applies.
Medication and daily life

The operator allows medication-assisted treatment. Methadone transfer must be arranged before intake. Stays can last up to two years. A 30-45-day initial adjustment period limits off-campus activity; outside employment begins no earlier than six months. Discuss the current rules and your prescriptions with the referral team.

name: Fort Lyon
bednote: Operator publishes capacity for up to 250 residents
cost: Housing reported free; confirm incidental and healthcare expenses.
residency: Colorado resident for at least six months; homeless or at risk of homelessness.
stay: Up to two years; provider referral required.
details: Bed count
The current operator referral page lists capacity for up to 250 people. This is the size of the residential community, not current openings.
Cost and admission

January 2026 reporting quotes the operator describing Fort Lyon and Sage Ridge as free to guests. Ask about incidental costs and healthcare coverage. Referral is through a case manager or service/healthcare provider. Applicants must voluntarily want recovery and meet residency, housing-instability, legal and medical criteria.
Stay and medical readiness

Stays can last up to two years. The current referral page asks for a 30-day supply of required medication plus a refill arrangement. Detox requirements must be satisfied safely before admission. Older linked materials give different medication and TB requirements; use the intake team's current instructions. Discuss mobility needs, prescriptions and safe withdrawal care with the referral team.

name: The Other Side Academy
people: Adults 18-64 | Residential work and recovery community
bednote: Current Denver total unverified after a 2025 housing expansion
cost: No program charge; substantial work commitment.
residency: Out-of-state policy not established in the reviewed pages. Ask Denver intake.
warning: Published psychiatric-medication and dual-diagnosis exclusions; no medical staff to monitor those needs.
details: Bed count

The earlier 70-person Denver figure was historical. A May 2025 report from the program's funder describes the opening of a house for 48 men in April 2025. That does not establish the total across today's Denver buildings. The old figure and new house are not added together. Current total capacity is unverified.
Commitment
The operator publishes no program fee and a 30-month stay with an intensive work and education schedule. Applicants generally must be 18-64 and able to participate.
Admission and medical fit

The judicial-information page explicitly excludes applicants requiring <q>psychological medication</q>, citing lack of medical staff. It also lists dual-diagnosis, sex-offense and arson exclusions. Confirm your individual eligibility and exact prescriptions with intake. Do not stop prescribed treatment to qualify.

details: Bed count

A current exact bed count for the long-term program was not established. The organization's profile describes more than 100 residents, which is not an exact capacity inventory. Annual clients and short-term Serenity beds are excluded.
Program length: confirmation needed

The dedicated long-term page says 2-3 years, with 30-day orientation + 17-month Phase 1 + six-month aftercare. The cost-of-care page calls it two years. Costs, work and healthcare

The dedicated long-term page includes treatment, room and board with no out-of-pocket financial commitment and describes at least a 40-hour workweek. The homepage uses the narrower phrase no up-front costs. Confirm all phases and charges. Ask about medication compatibility, withdrawal care, eligibility and the separate insurance/self-pay Serenity program.

name: CARITAS - The Healing Place
people: Men and women | Peer-led residential recovery
bednote: 225 in the current FAQ; older 2023 source totals 338. Current total unresolved.
cost: Free residential recovery; insurance not required or billed.
residency: Applicants may come from any state; admission screening still applies.
stay: Self-paced; education component typically 6-8 months, followed by workforce preparation.
warning: *225 is the operator FAQ figure used for sorting. Confirm current capacity and an available place.
details: Bed-count conflict

The current operator FAQ lists 225 residential recovery beds. A CARITAS presentation in Virginia's 2023 Abatement Academy lists 196 men's + 142 women's recovery beds = 338 on slide 16, separate from 64 emergency-shelter beds. A 2026 reopening announcement for the men's campus gives no new count. The discrepancy remains unresolved. The FAQ's 225 is a labeled sorting figure, not a verified current inventory.
Cost and admission

The Healing Place recovery program is free and does not bill private insurance or Medicaid. The operator explicitly permits applicants from anywhere. Contact the appropriate intake number. Separate emergency shelters and Recovery Residences apartments have different eligibility or cost arrangements.
Stay and medical services

The education component commonly takes 6-8 months, followed by a six-week workforce component; the whole stay can differ. The program advertises access to on-site medical, behavioral-health and opioid-use-disorder medication services. Confirm the exact prescription and intake needs before travel.

name: Delancey Street
people: Adults | Residential education and work community
bednote: 500-person housing design capacity; San Francisco campus only
cost: No entry fee; 50% of outside earnings covers costs in the final three months.
residency: No geographic restriction; acceptance is subject to screening.
stay: Minimum two years; internal work is unpaid.
warning: Published psychiatric-medication and dual-diagnosis exclusions; no professional clinical counseling.
details: Bed count
The operator describes its San Francisco complex as housing designed for 500 people. This is design capacity, not a current staffed-bed or vacancy inventory. Other campuses are excluded.
Cost and commitment

Minimum two years. Internal work is unpaid and supports the community. During the final three months before graduation, residents work outside: half of each paycheck is saved for their transition and half covers room, board and related program costs.
Medical fit and age

The operator describes resident ages as 18-68; this is not presented as a firm age cutoff. It excludes dual-diagnosis applicants and people requiring psychiatric medication and says it does not provide professional counseling. Do not stop prescribed care to qualify; discuss compatible placements with your prescriber.

name: TROSA
bednote: Current total unverified; historical 275 describes one Durham campus
cost: Residential treatment and essential needs are free; no insurance required.
residency: Applicants from any state may apply; phone interview and acceptance required.
warning: Not a detox facility. Medication acceptance depends on the prescribed drug and formulation.
details: Bed count

The earlier 275 figure describes 1820 James Street in a page discussing a 2022 expansion permit and expected 2024 completion. It does not establish today's total across Durham and Winston-Salem. A daily service population and a separate expansion maximum are not added together or substituted for current capacity. The current bed total remains unverified.
Cost and admission

The residential program provides housing, food, clothing and treatment free of charge. No insurance or outside referral is required. Applicants must contact admissions themselves for an interview and medical, psychiatric and legal screening. Arrange travel only after acceptance. Separate continuing-care housing for graduates is described as low cost.
Medication and participation

TROSA is not a detox facility. Its current FAQ explicitly supports some medications for opioid-use disorder, including naltrexone and certain long-acting injectable formulations. Confirm your exact prescription and formulation rather than assuming every medicine is accepted. The program includes structured work/community assignments and limited family contact early in the stay.

details: Costs and work

The national FAQ describes generally free 180-day residential programming. It also states that some qualifying government-provided benefits may offset room, board and clothing. Participants are not employees and are not paid wages for work therapy. Ask for the center's written financial terms.
Eligibility and local variation

The national recovery page generally lists ages 21-65, with local variation. Confirm medication compatibility, medical readiness, out-of-state intake, required participation and personal expenses. A national network does not mean automatic eligibility at every center.
